title: Streams and Screens: Middle East
summary: Magnite’s latest study explores how audiences in the Middle East engage with streaming and what their viewing habits mean for advertisers seeking to connect with them.
body_markdown:
##


**Shared Viewing Extends CTV’s Impact:** Among respondents who stream on CTV, 83% regularly watch with others. Not only does co-viewing extend reach, but 75% say they also remember ads better when watching with other people. A strategy spanning CTV and mobile can build on that attention, with 73% of respondents saying repeated exposure across both screens increases their likelihood of engagement.


**Unmet Needs Point to Opportunities for Streaming Services:** Viewers want more family-friendly programming and locally produced content that reflects their regional culture. They also want better ad experiences, including fewer repetitive ads. These all play a role when viewers are considering a new service. In addition, 52% say they are most likely to sign up for a streaming service offering a lower-cost plan with ads, while 49% favour access to live sports and events. These preferences give services and advertisers clear ways to respond to audience demand.
